pages.title: Oslo biotech declines to name backer

blocks.h: Oslo biotech declines to name backer of 'sleep study'

blocks.p: OSLO. Halvorsen Biogenetics confirmed on Monday that it is running a study into memory and sleep, but would not say who is paying for it or where it is taking place.
The company's own ethics board has not been shown the protocol, according to two people familiar with its meetings. A spokesperson said the work was 'at an early stage and commercially sensitive'.

pages.title: Refrigerated container held for a second week

blocks.h: Singapore port: refrigerated container held for a second week

blocks.p: SINGAPORE. Customs officers at Pasir Panjang are still holding a refrigerated container that arrived on the MV Corellia, after it weighed more than three times what its paperwork declared.
The terminal's operator, Meridian Freight, said the hold was 'a routine paperwork matter'. The owner of the cargo has asked the court to stop the container being opened.
Port workers told the Wire that the gate cameras were out of service on the night a second, unmarked refrigerated truck left the terminal.

pages.title: Insurers deny keeping a shared blacklist

blocks.h: Insurers deny keeping a shared blacklist

blocks.p: TORONTO. Three of Canada's largest insurers have denied that they share a list of customers judged to be fraud risks, after a former claims adjuster said such a list exists and that people are added to it for complaining.
Corvane Mutual called the claim 'categorically untrue'. It declined to say whether it keeps a list of its own.
